item.text:
Use compactness via the product space
\[
X=V(F)^{V(G)},
\]
whose points are all vertex maps \(V(G)\to V(F)\). Give \(V(F)\) the finite discrete topology; then \(X\) is compact by Tychonoff’s theorem.

For each edge \(uv\in E(G)\), impose the closed constraint
\[
C_{uv}=\{\varphi\in X:\varphi(u)\varphi(v)\in E(F)\}.
\]
A graph homomorphism \(G\to F\) is precisely a point in \(\bigcap_{uv\in E(G)}C_{uv}\).

Organize the argument around two goals:

1. Show every finite family of edge constraints is simultaneously satisfiable by applying the hypothesis to the finite subgraph containing their endpoints.
2. Invoke compactness: the closed sets \(C_{uv}\) have the finite-intersection property, so their total intersection is nonempty.

The finiteness of \(V(F)\) is the essential input making the discrete target compact.
